# SEC filing-index ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), in the existing uv workspace.
Choices made: Azure platform per the ADR (Proposed 2026-10-05; acceptance is spec §7 step 1).

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes for a configured quarter range, downloaded with original bytes kept | §2.1, §4.2, R1 | A | 1 | About 2 requests per quarter (listing + master.idx): 100 quarters ≈ 200 requests ≈ 70 s at 3 req/s (§4.3); bytes and time measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | Daily indexes ingested continuously, catching up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries | §2.1, §4.2, R2 | A | 2 | About 250 daily files a year plus quarter listings; negligible against 3 req/s |
| O3 | A canonical filing-index dataset in Parquet built from the ingested indexes | §2.1, §4.5, §4.6, R3 | A | 3 | Compute and peak memory measured by Stage 1 |
| O4 | The pipeline running on Azure (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Monitor) with runbooks | §4.1, §4.7, §4.9, §7, §8, R4 | A | 4 | Azure spend cannot be estimated before deployment; measured by the Stage 8 smoke test (§7 step 4) |
| O5 | Backfill, daily ingestion and reconciliation sharing one downloader, parser and publisher | §4.1, §6, R5 | A | 5 | No material cost beyond its stage |
| O6 | Rebuilding the catalog from stored bytes after a parser change, with no new download | §4.3, §4.5, §4.6, R6 | A | 6 | Zero SEC requests (§4.3); storage ≈ raw size × retained snapshots, raw size from Stage 1 |
| O7 | Periodic reconciliation of quarterly indexes against the published catalog | §4.2, §4.4, R7 | A | 7 | Each run re-reads every supported quarter: about O1's request count per week |
| O8 | All SEC traffic under one request budget, whatever the worker count | §4.3, R8 | A | 8 | No material cost |
| O9 | Readers finding each quarter's current dataset through one active pointer | §4.5, §4.6, R9 | A | 9 | One Parquet copy per retained generation; retention policy decides |
| O10 | Records withdrawn only after approval tied to a source hash; failures never remove records | §4.4, R10 | A | 10 | Operator time per approval; frequency unknown until reconciliation runs |
| O11 | Schedules, retry limits and the rate target held as reviewed configuration, in scheduled operation | §4.8, §7, §10, R11 | A | 11 | Partner review time per change |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression). Ranking confirmed 2026-11-06.

## Stages

Order follows the ranking except: O7 waits for O8 and O9, which it needs; O5 moves to
Stage 7, the first point where all three modes exist; O4 moves to Stage 8, as spec §7
also places deployment after the shared worker is built.

- [ ] Stage 1: Core quarterly baseline, local
      Objective: Download a configured range of real archived quarterly indexes and produce canonical Parquet locally.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: nothing built (generated scaffolds only); an SEC User-Agent identity and a quarter range from your partner
      Produces: shared downloader, raw byte store, parser and sec-index-v1 Parquet writer; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1: every master.idx in the range stored by SHA-256 with URL, receipt time and byte count. O3: one Parquet output per quarter whose row count equals the source's data rows. Cost: findings record bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory, request count and achieved request rate of the real run.
      Leaves out: manifests → Stage 3; active pointer and generations → Stage 5; shared lease budget → Stage 4; full validation suite and traceability → Stage 7; deployment → Stage 8; scheduling → Stage 9
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Daily ingestion and catch-up
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily indexes from a handoff date, through outages and quarter boundaries.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1 downloader, parser and Parquet writer
      Produces: daily discovery with pending and failed sources tracked; open-quarter precedence over daily rows
      Exit: O2: a run from a handoff date in a past quarter ingests every listed daily index across the boundary; a repeat run reports no_new_sources; a listed file that fails to download stays pending and appears in the report.
      Leaves out: manifests → Stage 3; scheduling → Stage 9
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Source manifest, replay and resume
      Objective: Track source, snapshot and processing identity so work resumes and replays from raw bytes.
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stages 1–2 raw store and outputs
      Produces: manifests: source, snapshot, workset-binding, processing and attempt records; downloaded → transformed → published states
      Exit: O6: after a parser-version change, rebuilding Stage 1–2 quarters with SEC access disabled yields the same logical rows; unchanged hash and versions skip; an interrupted multi-file run resumes without re-downloading completed members.
      Leaves out: deployment on Table Storage → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: One SEC request budget
      Objective: Make every collector share one lease-coordinated request budget.
      Outcomes: O8
      Consumes: Stage 1 downloader; Stage 3 attempt records
      Produces: lease-coordinated collector with bounded retries, Retry-After handling and access-denial halt
      Exit: O8: concurrent backfill, daily and reconciliation-style collectors issue requests one at a time within the configured rate, retries included; lease loss stops requests; a 403 halts the run.
      Leaves out: deployment on Azure Storage → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Versioned publication
      Objective: Publish complete quarter generations behind a conditionally updated active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 3 processing states
      Produces: generation manifests, changes output and a per-quarter active pointer with conditional writes
      Exit: O9: a reader that resolves the pointer gets one complete generation's file list; a crash before the pointer update leaves the previous generation readable; a competing publisher fails with a conflict, never an overwrite.
      Leaves out: deployment on Table Storage → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, apply safe changes, and gate withdrawals on hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stages 3–5
      Produces: reconciliation workflow, change reports, approval records
      Exit: O7: a reconciliation run re-reads every supported quarter, records additions and updates, and skips unchanged snapshots. O10: a closed-quarter candidate that removes keys stays awaiting_approval until an approval names its hash and generation; open-quarter absence and HTTP failures withdraw nothing.
      Leaves out: scheduled reconciliation → Stage 9
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Validation and recovery hardening
      Objective: Prove all three modes share one implementation and meet the CI exit criteria.
      Outcomes: O5
      Consumes: Stages 1–6
      Produces: full validation suite on committed fixtures, including legacy formats in the chosen range; traceability: durable run reports and structured logs
      Exit: O5: the §6 CI exit criteria pass without any SEC download, with backfill, daily and reconciliation exercising the same downloader, parser and publisher; run reports carry §4.7 counts and gaps.
      Leaves out: Azure integration tests and alerts → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 8: Azure deployment
      Objective: Run the shared worker on Azure in an isolated environment with triggers disabled.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stage 7 suite; ADR and spec accepted, and §7 step 1 values recorded
      Produces: deployment: versioned infrastructure, managed identities, ADF pipelines, Container Apps Jobs, alerts and runbooks; smoke-test record
      Exit: O4: ADF starts and polls jobs running all four commands against ADLS and Table Storage under managed identity; integration and fault-injection tests pass; a one-quarter and one-daily-index smoke test is recorded and replays unchanged with SEC access disabled.
      Leaves out: scheduling and trigger enablement → Stage 9
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 9: Baseline and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the production backfill and catch-up, then enable the daily and weekly triggers.
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stage 8 deployment
      Produces: scheduling: enabled triggers under reviewed configuration; release record
      Exit: O11: reviewed configuration deployed; the baseline is complete, or an approved incomplete range is recorded; the triggers are enabled after catch-up and a manual reconciliation; observed scheduled runs match their reports; the release record names image digest, configuration revision and active generations.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

When every stage is ticked, run SKILL.md §6 over the Outcomes list, with evidence per
verdict. Every numbered spec requirement (R1–R11) is cited by an outcome's `Spec` cell;
list any found uncited as unmet. Unmet items exit as a new stage or a deferral with a
written reason.
